jobs.company: Pacific Door Systems Ltd · ASSA ABLOY
jobs.summary: Lead the end-to-end finance function for Pacific Door Systems, covering management accounts, budgets, forecasts, cash flow, statutory payments and group reporting. The role is full-time and onsite in either Auckland or Wellington.
jobs.company_intro: ASSA ABLOY is a global access solutions business serving residential, commercial and institutional markets. Pacific Door Systems is the business covered by this role.
jobs.description_html:
About Us

ASSA ABLOY is the global leader in access solutions, trusted in over 70 countries to deliver smart, secure and seamless experiences.

Through our portfolio of trusted brands and access solutions, we help create secure, safe and convenient environments across residential, commercial and institutional markets.

Backed by global expertise and local support, we continue to set the benchmark for innovation, reliability and performance.


About the Role

Reporting to the General Manager of the Pacific Doors, the Finance Manager is responsible for timely, relevant, accurate, and high-quality planning, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting to support the business. You will ensure the day-to-day accounting operations are completed accurately and demonstrate best practice, whilst ensuring regulatory and legal compliance.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • End-to-end finance function for Pacific Door Systems Ltd

  • Ensure that all statutory payments are made accurately and on time. PAYE, FBT, Provisional Tax, ACC, GST etc.

  • Produce accurate and fully reconciled monthly management accounts by the due date the following month.

  • Manage monthly reporting, budgeting, strategic planning financials, forecast, and cash flow.

  • Ability to interpret and work with standard costing models.

  • Complete all group reporting requirements including HFM reporting.

  • Produce accurate and fully reconciled year-end accounts.

  • Review, approve and pay weekly wages, monthly creditors, and all other required payments.

  • Manage relationships with our Bank Manager and Tax Accountants.

  • Other ad-hoc tasks and projects as required.


Location & Working Arrangements

This role is an onsite position and can be based in either Auckland or Wellington, New Zealand.


About You

We are looking for an experienced Finance leader who has experience in a manufacturing environment. You will possess the ability to work well in a team environment, act decisively and deliver consistently. Further, you will possess:

  • Tertiary qualification in accounting or equivalent and CA/CPA qualified

  • Minimum of five years post qualification experience

  • An in-depth understanding of fiscal management, processes, and reporting

  • Substantial experience in accounting systems

  • Traditional accounting expertise with a good working knowledge of accounting systems and principles and relevant legislation

  • Proven effective leadership and staff management skills

  • Excellent stakeholder management skills and ability to communicate effectively with Senior Leaders.


Diversity, Equity & Inclusion

At ASSA ABLOY, we believe our people make us stronger. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences and perspectives and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive.

If you require reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know.


Recruitment Process & How to Apply

If you're ready to take the next step in your finance career, we'd love to hear from you.

Applicants must have valid New Zealand working rights at the time of application.

As part of our recruitment process, shortlisted candidates will be required to complete pre-employment screening, including reference checks, confirmation of working rights, Ministry of Justice (MOJ) and police checks, and, where appropriate, financial and credit-related background checks.

Any offer of employment will be subject to the satisfactory completion of these checks.

jobs.description_html:
The Opportunity:

We are looking for a hands-on, technically strong Finance Manager to join our Support Office Finance Team and work closely with the CFO to deliver accurate reporting, strong balance sheet control, and meaningful financial insight across the business.

This full-time role reports to the CFO and has one direct report, the Assistant Accountant. You will manage the month-end close, tax compliance, treasury activity, inventory accounting and day-to-day finance operations, while helping simplify, automate and document finance processes. A key focus will be taking ownership of monthly balance sheet reconciliations and providing the financial visibility the business needs to make good decisions.

Key responsibilities include (but not limited to):

  • Manage the month-end close, including journals with clear supporting workings, and deliver timely, accurate monthly reporting, including P&L, balance sheet, cash flow and variance analysis.

  • Own monthly balance sheet reconciliations and inventory accounting, ensuring balances are supported and issues are resolved promptly.

  • Provide monthly reporting, commentary and insights to the CFO, leadership team and branch P&L owners.

  • Support the CFO with monthly Board and shareholder reporting, including treasury and cash flow commentary.

  • Review GST, FBT and PAYE returns, support the annual income tax return and ensure compliance with NZ IFRS, New Zealand tax legislation and company accounting policies.

  • Facilitate the external audit and support completion of annual statutory accounts within agreed timelines.

  • Manage daily cash flow forecasting, banking activity and debtor finance facility reporting.

  • Lead the annual budget and reforecasts in partnership with the CFO.

  • Simplify, automate and document finance processes, building strong controls as the business grows.

  • Lead, coach and develop the Assistant Accountant.

About You:

You will be a proactive, self-sufficient finance professional who is comfortable working in the detail while also providing clear advice to senior leaders and operational stakeholders. You will bring strong technical accounting capability, sound judgement and the credibility to represent the finance function across the business.

  • Business degree in accounting, finance or a related discipline, or equivalent.

  • CA ANZ or CPA qualified (or nearing completion).

  • Minimum five years' experience in a senior finance role.

  • Proven month-end close, management reporting, budgeting and forecasting experience, with the ability to meet tight deadlines.

  • Practical understanding of NZ IFRS and New Zealand tax legislation.

  • Advanced Excel skills and experience using ERP accounting software for reporting and analysis; Oracle experience would be advantageous.

  • Excellent communication, stakeholder management and relationship-building skills.

  • Experience leading, coaching or developing others.

What We Offer:

  • Staff purchasing benefits

  • Holiday home subsidies

  • Birthday Leave

  • Ongoing training and professional development

  • Supportive and collaborative team environment

For almost 90 years, Ideal Electrical has provided outstanding service and solutions to electrical professionals. Our extensive nationwide network from Whangārei to Invercargill services the electrical supply needs of the residential, commercial and industrial sectors, providing technologically advanced products in lighting, data and solar.

But what really sets us apart?

We believe in the Power of Connection — making experiences easy for our customers and each other. When you join us, you’re not just taking a job. You’re joining a team that values relationships, growth, and doing great work together.

Ready to make an impact?

If you enjoy improving processes, leading month-end delivery and partnering with stakeholders across the business, we would like to hear from you! Apply now with your CV and cover letter.

Applications will be reviewed as they are received with the aim of filling this role as soon as possible. Please note: Applicants must have a legal right to work in New Zealand.

Newly Developed role- Financial Accountant

Join a New Zealand Icon and Help Shape the Future

If you're looking for a role where you can combine technical accounting expertise with genuine business influence, we'd love to hear from you.

This isn't just another Financial Accountant position. You'll have the opportunity to work across the business, influence decision-making, improve systems and processes, and help shape the future of a company that has been protecting New Zealanders for more than 140 years.

Who are we?

At Wormald, we're more than New Zealand's leading fire protection company. We help protect people, property, and businesses across the country through innovative fire protection solutions and exceptional service.

With over 140 years of history behind us, we're now focused on the future. As our business continues to evolve, we're looking for a commercially minded Financial Accountant who wants to do more than produce numbers. This is an opportunity to influence decisions, improve systems and processes, and help drive the financial performance of a nationally recognized organization.

Why Join us?

  • Competitive salary package - We recognize and reward capability and performance.

  • Subsidized healthcare - Helping you and your family stay healthy and supported.

  • On-site parking - Convenient and hassle-free parking available.

  • Career growth opportunities - Be part of a business investing in people, process improvement, and future leadership capability.

  • Make an impact - Work closely with senior leaders and operational teams to influence business outcomes.

  • Stability and purpose - Join New Zealand's leading fire protection business and help protect what matters most.

About the Role

Reporting to the Finance Manager, you'll play a key role in ensuring the accuracy and integrity of Wormald's financial information while providing valuable commercial insights to support decision-making.

This is an excellent opportunity for a technically strong accountant who enjoys getting involved in the wider business, improving processes, and partnering with stakeholders to deliver results.

What You'll Be Doing

Financial Reporting & Analysis

  • Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports, including profit and loss, balance sheet, and cash flow statements.

  • Manage month-end close activities, journals, and balance sheet reconciliations.

  • Support budgeting, forecasting, and cash flow management.

  • Analyze financial performance and provide meaningful insights to business leaders.

Business Partnering

  • Work closely with operational and leadership teams across the business.

  • Translate financial data into practical recommendations.

  • Support cost management, profitability improvement, and strategic decision-making.

  • Help drive a strong commercial and performance-focused culture.

Compliance & Governance

  • Ensure compliance with accounting standards, taxation obligations, and internal policies.

  • Prepare GST and FBT returns.

  • Assist with external audits and statutory reporting requirements.

  • Maintain and strengthen financial controls and risk management practices.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to improve systems, reporting, and financial processes.

  • Support finance transformation and process improvement initiatives.

  • Contribute to the ongoing development of ERP and reporting capabilities.

What Success Looks Like

We're looking for someone who combines strong technical accounting capability with a proactive and commercially focused mindset. You'll be comfortable rolling up your sleeves when required while confidently engaging with managers and leaders across the business.

You'll Bring

  • Tertiary qualification in Accounting, Finance, or a related discipline.

  • CA, CPA, or equivalent qualification (or working towards completion).

  • Previous experience as a Financial Accountant or in a similar role.

  • Strong knowledge of month-end reporting, reconciliations, and financial controls.

  • Experience with GST, FBT, audits, and statutory compliance.

  • Advanced Excel skills and confidence working with ERP systems.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to build trusted relationships.

  • A continuous improvement mindset and desire to make a difference.

Experience within construction, project-based, service, contracting, or multi-branch businesses would be highly regarded.

What We're Looking For

Just as importantly, we're looking for someone who:

  • Takes ownership and accountability.

  • Enjoys improving processes and finding smarter ways of working.

  • Builds strong relationships across the business.

  • Thrives in a dynamic and evolving environment.

  • Wants to contribute to a positive and collaborative culture.

Salary & Benefits

At Wormald, we understand that great people deserve great rewards. We offer a competitive remuneration package and a range of benefits designed to support your wellbeing and career growth, including:

  • Competitive salary aligned to your skills and experience

  • Subsidized healthcare

  • On-site parking

  • Ongoing professional development and career progression opportunities

  • Exposure to senior leadership and commercial decision-making

  • The opportunity to contribute to a business undergoing growth and transformation

  • A supportive, collaborative, and values-driven team environment

Pre-Employment Requirements

The successful candidate will be required to complete:

  • Reference checks

  • Medical assessment

  • Criminal history check

  • Drug and alcohol screening

Ready to Join Us?

Apply today and become part of a company that protects people, property, and communities across New Zealand.

Tāmaki Paenga Hira: Tui tui hono tangata, whenua me te moana.

Auckland War Memorial Museum: Connecting through sharing stories of people, lands and seas

Auckland Museum is a much-loved culture and heritage organisation at the heart of Auckland's identity, committed to outstanding management of its world-class collections, developing and sharing engaging content through its galleries, exhibition, events, educational programmes and the permanent and volunteer staff who tell the Museum's stories. We are Auckland's home of commemoration as well as the country’s oldest research institution and a major tourist destination.


Mō te tūranga | About the role

Fixed-term Parental Leave cover | Full-Time

Our Head of Finance will be taking parental leave, and we're seeking an experienced finance leader to run operational finance through to September 2027. You'll own the day-to-day function and its team and work closely with our Director Enterprise, Finance, Property & Development, who leads financial strategy, governance and executive engagement across the Museum.

Reporting to the Director Enterprise, Finance, Property & Development, you will lead an established finance team of 6 professionals and play a pivotal role in maintaining financial performance, supporting governance reporting and partnering with leaders across a complex and dynamic organisation.

The Museum is at the start of an ambitious capital transformation programme that will shape it for generations. You'll play a key role in establishing the financial management foundations that support its success, including forecasting, controls, reporting and business partnering with teams responsible for delivery.

What the role is about

  • Owning the numbers - You understand what sits behind every figure and ensure reporting and decision-making are built on robust analysis and trusted information.
  • Running the function - You'll lead and develop the Finance team, resolve technical issues and ensure the function delivers high-quality service across the Museum
  • Leading the business financially - You'll provide insight, challenge assumptions and help managers make informed decisions that support organisational outcomes.
  • Planning ahead and adapting - You'll keep Finance focused on what's ahead, while remaining agile enough to respond to changing organisational priorities.

Your remit will cover monthly reporting and forecasting, budgeting, treasury management, year-end financial statements and audit, financial controls, insurance, finance systems and commercial support to leaders across the Museum.

What’s in it for you

  • Real leadership responsibility – lead operational finance for one of Aotearoa's most recognised institutions with ownership of the function and day-to-day decision-making.
  • A formative role in a major capital programme – help establish the financial management framework for a transformation programme from the outset.
  • Governance exposure – prepare reporting and papers for the Executive Team, Trust Board and Audit & Risk Committee and gain insight into strategic decision-making.
  • Unusual breadth – work across public funding, commercial operations, philanthropy, grant funding and investment funds in a single organisation.
  • Direct access to the CFO – work closely with a senior leader whose portfolio spans finance, property, commercial activity and fundraising.
  • Purpose-driven work – help safeguard the financial sustainability of an institution that protects and shares the stories, collections and taonga of Auckland and Aotearoa

Qualifications and Experience

  • Chartered Accountant (CAANZ) or equivalent professional qualification
  • Experience leading, or acting as second-in-charge of, a finance function within a complex organisation
  • Strong technical expertise in financial reporting, audit and financial controls
  • Proven experience coaching and developing high-performing teams
  • Commercial curiosity and the ability to translate financial information into meaningful insights for non-financial stakeholder
